notes:
Refresh looks like a button
specula guards the vault better

entries.title: Refresh looks like a button
entries.detail: The dashboard's Refresh is now an amber button like the ones in the header. While the figures are being read, it says Reading… and its arrows turn, where before it only went grey. specula's server now runs on Node 24.22.1, with the security fixes of 21 October.

entries.title: specula guards the vault better
entries.detail: specula's page and its reports now run only specula's own code and send nothing to other sites, even if a note or a report held some. A link in a report that would run code shows as words. A broken address no longer stops specula's server.

entries.title: One defect is "1 defect"
entries.detail: A knowledge base's card on the dashboard wrote "1 defects" when verify.py found one. It now writes "1 defect".

entries.title: No blue marks on the page after the quick lookup
entries.detail: Opening the quick lookup could select all the text of specula's page, which then showed in blue in the header and the search bar. It no longer does.

entries.title: The quick lookup without the mark again
entries.detail: The mark and the name above the quick lookup's field are gone again. It shows its 8 results at once, with no scroll bar, and is as tall as they need, with the same space above the first as below the last.

entries.title: The quick lookup shows all its results at once
entries.detail: The quick lookup is taller and shows all 8 results at once, with no scroll bar. Each result shows its title, one line and the path of its page, without the stable, unverified and stale labels. In Settings › Mac app, its hotkey is now under Hotkey, as Look up in 00_Cerebrum.

entries.title: The quick lookup searches as you type
entries.detail: Type the first letters of a word, and the quick lookup shows the concepts with words that start with them: "kerb" finds Kerberos. Before, it needed the whole word.

entries.title: Ask Claude finds concepts faster
entries.detail: Ask Claude now looks a concept up in the vault's own index, as the quick lookup does, before it searches any file. On three test questions it answered about a fifth faster, with a quarter fewer steps, for about a fifth less money.

entries.title: The quick lookup's hotkey is in Settings
entries.detail: Settings › Mac app shows the quick lookup's keys, ⌃⌥⌘C, under Quick lookup. Click them, then press new keys to choose others, as for Open specula.

entries.title: No dark frame around the page and the dashboard
entries.detail: A concept page and the dashboard now sit on the same grey as the header, the search bar and the list on the left, with one thin line between them, as the header has. The dark gap around them is gone.

entries.title: Reports: summaries, quotes and lines drawn right
entries.detail: A report's management summary starts with its Problem row, no longer drawn as a heading you could sort by. A quote shows as a quote, with a bar on its left and without the ">" marks. A line between parts is a line, not "---". A note the writer left for the next writer is no longer shown.

entries.title: The dashboard is a card too
entries.detail: The dashboard now sits on a card, as a concept page does: white in the light look, a lighter grey in the dark look. Its own cards are one quiet step lighter inside it.

entries.title: A concept page is a card
entries.detail: A concept page now sits on a card, as in folia: white in the light look, a lighter grey in the dark look, with a thin border and round corners. Before, its text sat on the window's darkest grey.

entries.title: The 00_Cerebrum Dashboard: click a figure
entries.detail: The dashboard is called 00_Cerebrum Dashboard. Click a figure to see what it counts, right under it: the stale and the draft pages, the open and deferred items, a red verify.py's lines. A page in that list opens with a click. Concepts opens the concept list at that base, and the health check's date opens its report. A small arrow shows which figures open.

entries.title: No table scrolls sideways
entries.detail: A table too wide for a concept page now fits it: a path may break after a slash, the cells get a little smaller, and only then may a long word break. No page scrolls sideways any more. The two buttons on a concept page have the same corners as the header's.

entries.title: The dashboard follows the style guide
entries.detail: The dashboard's title has the size of a concept page's title, without the line under it. Card titles have the guide's weight. File names in Needs you sit in the guide's code box. The lower cards stand in the same three columns as the cards above, so their edges line up.

entries.title: No scrollbar on the dashboard
entries.detail: The dashboard draws no scrollbar. It still scrolls with the trackpad, the mouse wheel and the keys.

entries.title: The dashboard's lists: no scrollbars, easier to read
entries.detail: The three cards at the bottom of the dashboard grow to hold their text and never scroll. Changed since yesterday is on the left, Needs you in the middle and wider, Stale on the right. A long list shows twelve rows and a Show all button. In Needs you, each item shows the file it is about, its question in bold, then short paragraphs, and the readings as a numbered list.

entries.title: Every knowledge base on the dashboard
entries.detail: The dashboard has room for every knowledge base, three to a row, in the same order as the header. NZZ and SRG SSR are marked frozen. They show as soon as the vault's dashboard script lists them.

entries.title: Look up the vault from any app: ⌃⌥⌘C
entries.detail: Press ⌃⌥⌘C anywhere, or choose Look Up in the Vault… in the menu, and type a name or a few words; "who is Robi" works too. The best concepts show at once, each with a line of what it is, its path, and how far to trust it: its status, whether it was checked, and stale when it is past its date. Return or a click opens the concept in specula. It uses no model and nothing leaves the Mac. Escape puts it away.

entries.title: Reports: key figures as tiles, tables that sort
entries.detail: A report with a Key figures section shows each figure as a tile. Click a tile to see the sources its number came from; a path in them opens that concept. Click a column's head to sort a table, again for the other way, a third time for the order as written. The Sources at the end are folded: open them with a click, or follow a footnote mark.

entries.title: A dashboard: how the vault stands
entries.detail: specula now opens on a dashboard, the first of the view buttons. It shows whether verify.py is green, each live knowledge base's figures, and three lists: what needs you, what goes stale in the next 30 days, and what changed since yesterday. A row opens its concept or report. A red verify.py shows red. The figures take about half a minute to read; Refresh reads them again.

entries.title: Reports looks the same way
entries.detail: The Reports button at the end of the search bar is a soft amber square too. It is full amber while the Reports window is open.

entries.title: Search and Ask look the same way
entries.detail: The Search and Ask buttons in the search bar are soft amber squares too, like the header's. The lit one is full amber.

entries.title: The header's buttons look like tabula's New task
entries.detail: The view buttons and Settings are small soft amber squares now. Point at one and its edge lights. The view that shows, and Settings while it is open, are full amber.

entries.title: Get the Mac app is now in About
entries.detail: Settings › About specula now holds the download of the Mac app. In a browser the Mac app part is gone, as it held nothing else. In the Mac app, that part keeps its hotkey, its icon and opening at login.

entries.title: The Timelapse builds from behind the ship
entries.detail: The Timelapse now starts from the view the 3D view opens on: SRG SSR builds on the left, NZZ on the right, ETH in front. The camera floats in a small loop and rises, comes down behind the ship for the warp, and rests on the same view at the end.

entries.title: Settings › Mac app as in folia
entries.detail: The part has the same groups and words as in folia: Hotkey, This Mac and Get the Mac app. "Start specula at login" is called "Open at login" again.

entries.title: No scrollbar in Settings
entries.detail: About specula now fits the window: the build facts stand in two columns, what each one means is in its tooltip, and Where your notes live has two short rows. Settings draws no scrollbar.

entries.title: Settings as big as tabula's; more in About
entries.detail: The Settings window has the size of tabula's. About specula lists the build code, build number, build date, the first commit, the web app and the Mac app, and says where your notes live. A new part, Account, shows who uses specula on this Mac and the vault it reads.

entries.title: A new icon: the eye
entries.detail: specula's app icon, menu bar icon, disk image and browser tab now show an eye: a lookout watching. The old mark was too fine at small sizes; the eye stays clear in the menu bar. Inside specula, the header and Settings › About keep the vault's mark.

entries.title: 3D opens behind the ship
entries.detail: Switched to 3D, the vault now turns to the view from behind the ship and a little above, as in the warp: ITAKB and ITKB at the top, ETH and kedavra in the middle, SRG SSR and NZZ at the bottom. The Timelapse keeps its own view.

entries.title: Other apps can open specula on a view
entries.detail: A link specula://show with a view of the vault brings the specula Mac app to the front on that view. GLaDOS uses it to show you the Cerebrum in specula, not in a browser tab.

entries.title: About and What's New in the family's style
entries.detail: About and What's New in the Mac app follow the folia style guide now, as Settings does: a head, a body of soft cards, and a foot with the buttons on the right. Done is the one amber button.

entries.title: A concept page uses its width, in the style guide's colours
entries.detail: A concept page's text now fills the page's column, as its tables do, and no table runs past it: a very wide one scrolls sideways inside the page. The colours follow folia's style guide: titles and headings in the text colour, amber only for links and what is selected, and every text easy to read in light and dark.

entries.title: The whole of specula follows the family's style guide
entries.detail: The header, the list, the concept page, the search bar and the card beside the map now use the sizes, weights and corners of folia's style guide, in the Mac's own font, as Settings does. The concept page's text is 14.5 px. The first row of categories stays on one line again in a 1440 px window, and hiding a knowledge base no longer moves the chips beside it.

entries.title: Settings and the windows follow the family's style guide
entries.detail: Settings, About, ⌘K and the Reports window now look as folia's style guide says: the Mac's own font, one base size, the small buttons of every Settings row 30 px high, and amber text and focus rings a little darker, so they read well on every light ground. The red Delete button reads well in dark mode too.

entries.title: Docs in Settings opens the manual in a window
entries.detail: In the specula Mac app, Settings › About specula › Docs opens the specula Field Manual in a window of the app, as the Docs button in the About specula window does. In a browser it still opens the page online.

entries.title: About specula has Settings…
entries.detail: About specula now has the buttons every app of the family has, in the same order: Docs, What's New… and Settings…, which opens specula's Settings the way the menu does.

entries.title: Docs opens the manual inside specula
entries.detail: About specula › Docs now shows the specula Field Manual in a window of specula's own, from the copy specula carries. It needs no claude.ai account and no internet, so anyone who has specula can read it. A link to the web in the manual opens in your browser.
